study_name.notes: Study has no formal name; refers to methotrexate impact on gut microbiota

subject_id.notes: Only named donors identified; de-identified patient IDs not provided in text

sample_id.notes: Samples referenced as stool samples but specific sample identifiers not provided in main text

curator.notes: Not applicable; paper is primary publication, not a curated dataset

pmid.notes: PubMed ID provided in paper header

subcohort.notes: Responder status only for RA patient cohort; germ-free mouse experiments use donor-based stratification

value: effects of methotrexate on gut microbiota
target_condition.evidence_quote: Methotrexate impacts conserved pathways in diverse human gut bacteria
target_condition.notes: Primary phenotype is RA; secondary focus is MTX-induced microbiota changes

control.notes: Donor 1 described as healthy; all other donors have rheumatoid arthritis

country.evidence_quote: New York University Langone Medical Center's rheumatology clinics
country.section: Methods - NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
country.notes: RA patients recruited from New York University; Donor 1 location not specified

body_site.evidence_quote: stool samples collected from a healthy human male
body_site.section: Results - Methotrexate has a broad impact
body_site.notes: All human samples are fecal/stool samples; mouse cecal and colon tissue also analyzed

body_site_details.notes: Only 'stool' mentioned; no specific anatomical subsites for fecal collection

days_from_first_collection.evidence_quote: stool samples collected at baseline and 1 month after treatment initiation
days_from_first_collection.notes: Baseline sample at day 0; post-treatment at approximately day 30 for RA patients

lifestyle.notes: Not applicable; study participants are from westernized healthcare setting

location.evidence_quote: New York University Langone Medical Center
location.section: Methods - NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
location.notes: Location provided for RA patient recruitment; Donor 1 location not specified

probing_pocket_depth.notes: Not applicable; study focuses on rheumatoid arthritis, not periodontal disease

westernized.evidence_quote: patients from New York University rheumatology clinics
westernized.notes: RA patients recruited from westernized healthcare setting in New York City

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: recent (<3 months prior) use of any antibiotic therapy
antibiotics_exclusion_period.section: Methods - NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
antibiotics_exclusion_period.notes: Exclusion criterion for RA patient cohort

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: recent (<3 months prior) use of any antibiotic therapy
antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.section: Methods - NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition

probing_pocket_depth_value.notes: Not applicable; study does not measure periodontal probing depth

dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods - NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
dna_extraction_kit.notes: MoBio PowerSoil kit used for human fecal DNA extraction

sequencing_platform.section: Methods - 16S-seq of humanized mouse gut microbiota
sequencing_platform.notes: MiSeq used for 16S rRNA sequencing; NovaSeq used for shotgun metagenomic sequencing

age.notes: Age not reported in main text; may be in supplementary tables

age_group.section: Methods - NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
age_group.notes: Inclusion criterion specifies ≥18 years; likely Adult but not explicitly stated

age_unit.notes: Not applicable; specific age values not reported

ancestry.notes: Ancestry not reported in main text

ancestry_details.notes: Ethnicity mentioned as collected (Table S1C) but specific values not in main text

family.notes: Not applicable; individual participants, not family-based sampling

family_role.notes: Not applicable; family roles not relevant to this study design

sex.evidence_quote: healthy human male (Donor 1); treatment-naïve female and male donors with rheumatoid arthritis
sex.notes: Sex specified for named donors; RA patient cohort sex composition not reported for responder/non-responder groups

age_min.notes: Age information for humans not reported; gnotobiotic mice ages 6-16 weeks.

age_years.notes: Human participant ages not reported in abstract or methods.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: recent (<3 months prior) use of any antibiotic therapy
antibiotics_current_use.section: Methods — Human RA patient samples acquisition
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion: participants must not have used antibiotics within 3 months prior to enrollment.

dietary_restriction.notes: Extreme diets excluded (e.g., parenteral nutrition, macrobiotic diet) but no specific dietary restrictions reported for included participants.

disease.evidence_quote: Consecutive patients from the New York University Langone Medical Center's rheumatology clinics and offices were screened for the presence of RA based on ACR criteria
disease.section: Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
disease.notes: Study includes healthy donor (Donor 1) and treatment-naïve RA patients (Donors 2, 3).

disease_details.evidence_quote: New-onset RA was defined as disease duration of a minimum of 6 weeks and up to 6 months since diagnosis
disease_details.section: Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition

disease_response_orr.notes: ORR not applicable; study uses DAS28 response criterion instead.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Not applicable to rheumatoid arthritis study.

disease_response_recist.notes: RECIST not applicable to RA; DAS28 response used instead.

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool samples collected but phenotypic characteristics not reported.

fmt_id.evidence_quote: Mice were colonized with stool from human donors, either a healthy male donor or a treatment-naïve (re-MTX) female and male donors
fmt_id.notes: Donor identifiers assigned for tracking in FMT experiments.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: Germ-free mice were colonized with pre- and post-treatment stool samples from the 3 MTX-Rs
fmt_role.section: Results — The post-treatment microbiome decreases host immune activation
fmt_role.notes: Human donors provided stool for fecal microbiota transplantation into germ-free mice.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Not applicable; study involves adult RA patients and germ-free mice.

smoker.notes: Smoking status not reported in paper.

treatment.evidence_quote: Patients received oral MTX at standard of care doses as prescribed by their treating rheumatologists.
treatment.section: Methods — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
treatment.notes: MTX dosing specifics: low-dose 1 mg/kg or high-dose 50 mg/kg used in mouse experiments; human patients received standard oral MTX doses.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not applicable; study focuses on RA, not cancer.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Bacteroidetes decreased and Actinobacteria increased; DAS28 score; purine and pyrimidine metabolism; B220+, CD44+ CD69+ CD4+, Gr1+ CD11b+ cells
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified throughout the study; some are taxonomic (Bacteroidetes), clinical (DAS28), molecular (gene families), or immunological (cell populations)

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: fold change percentage in which values are normalized to pre-MTX group
biomarker_unit.section: Methods — Analysis of immune cell markers
biomarker_unit.notes: Units not universally reported; immune cell measurements expressed as fold change relative to pre-MTX controls

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Bacteroidetes decreased; DAS28 score improved by at least 1.8; fold change 0.48–1.3 in unchallenged; 0.64–1.33 in challenged
biomarker_value.section: Results — Clinical relevance and Immune activation
biomarker_value.notes: Values represent changes observed post-MTX treatment or between responders and non-responders

disease_response_os.notes: Overall survival data not reported; study focuses on microbiota response and immune activation, not patient survival

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not assessed or reported in this study

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: High-dose MTX significantly decreased the Bacteroidetes phylum; altered 14 bacterial genera and 81 ASVs; significant decrease in richness
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Multiple fecal microbiota phenotypes measured via 16S-seq and shotgun metagenomics

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Tumor size measurements not relevant to this microbiota and immunology study

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Residual tumor measurement not assessed; study focuses on RA, not cancer

value: MTX doses used: 1 mg/kg (low-dose) and 50 mg/kg (high-dose) in gnotobiotic mice
Clinical MTX dosing: standard of care doses prescribed by rheumatologists
MTX-responder defined as DAS28 decrease ≥1.8 with continued oral MTX without biologics
Inflammatory trigger: 2% DSS (dextran sodium sulfate) in drinking water for 6–8 days
Study included 45 bacterial isolates from 6 phyla
30 MTX-naïve RA patients for ex vivo studies
23 RA patients with longitudinal 16S-seq data (baseline and 1 month post-MTX)
17 RA patients with shotgun metagenomic sequencing
Germ-free mice colonized with human stool and treated with MTX or vehicle
MTX estimated GI tract concentration: 22–220 μM (10–100 μg/ml) in proximal GI tract
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: low-dose MTX (1 mg/kg) or high-dose MTX (50 mg/kg); standard of care doses; DAS28 decrease of ≥1.8; 2% DSS in drinking water; 45 bacterial isolates; 30 MTX-naïve patients; 23 RA patients at baseline and 1 month; estimated concentration of MTX in the proximal gastrointestinal tract (22–220 μM or 10–100 μg/ml)
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive metadata on experimental design, patient populations, dosing regimens, and analytical approaches

host_species.evidence_quote: germ-free mice colonized with human stool; consecutive patients from NYU Langone; C57BL/6J mice females ages 6–16 weeks
host_species.section: Methods — Experimental Model and Subject Details
host_species.notes: Study used both human RA patients and gnotobiotic mice (C57BL/6J) colonized with human microbiota
